acceptance_condition: Returns at least three design constraints, each explicitly labeled as 'design inference', that specify how the Dung notions map to the Q/A graph, including concrete edge types and semantics. Each must be grounded in the extracted definitions but must not be presented as source claims.
rationale: This child directly addresses D3 (answer-to-answer conflict/provenance relations) and D8 (contradiction behavior) by translating the formal definitions into design constraints for the graph substrate.
text: Derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, how Dung's notions of argumentation framework, acceptability, conflict-free sets, and admissible sets can anchor answer-to-answer conflict and provenance relations in a many-to-many question/answer graph. Specifically, produce at least three design constraints: (1) how to model answers as arguments and conflicts as attack edges; (2) how to represent provenance relations (e.g., answer-addresses-question) as additional graph edges that do not alter conflict semantics; and (3) how admissible sets can define mutually consistent answer sets for a given question.
